beats.lead: The headlines all said the same thing
beats.text: It was not one prize for one idea.
beats.note: The 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was split in half: one half for predicting the shape of proteins that already exist, the other for designing entirely new ones that don't.

beats.name: Demis Hassabis and John Jumper
beats.role: Their AI model AlphaFold2 solved a problem chemists had chased for over fifty years: working out a protein's 3D shape from its amino acid sequence alone.

beats.context: Roughly how many protein structures AlphaFold2 has predicted, against about 200,000 solved across sixty years of X-ray crystallography before it.

beats.lead: The other half of the same prize
beats.text: David Baker builds proteins that never existed.
beats.note: Starting with a protein called Top7 in 2003, his lab designs entirely new structures from scratch, not variations on ones nature already made.

beats.text: One half reads life's code. The other half writes new lines in it.

beats.line: Two different breakthroughs. One shared afternoon in Stockholm.
